contents.html: Abstract
contents.html_ja: 概要

contents.html: This publication describes cryptographic methods that are approved for “key wrapping,” i.e., the protection of the confidentiality and integrity of cryptographic keys. In addition to describing existing methods, this publication specifies two new, deterministic authenticated-encryption modes of operation of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm: the AES Key Wrap (KW) mode and the AES Key Wrap With Padding (KWP) mode. An analogous mode with the Triple Data Encryption Algorithm (TDEA) as the underlying block cipher, called TKW, is also specified, to support legacy applications.
contents.html_ja: 本刊行物は、「鍵ラッピング」、すなわち暗号鍵の機密性および完全性の保護のために承認された暗号方式を説明します。既存の方式の説明に加え、本刊行物は、Advanced Encryption Standard（AES）アルゴリズムの、決定論的な認証付き暗号化の利用モードを2つ新たに規定します。AES Key Wrap（KW）モードと AES Key Wrap With Padding（KWP）モードです。また、レガシーアプリケーションをサポートするため、基礎となるブロック暗号として Triple Data Encryption Algorithm（TDEA）を用いる同様のモードであるTKWも規定します。

contents.html: 3 Introduction
contents.html_ja: 3 はじめに

contents.html: 3.1 Overview
contents.html_ja: 3.1 概要

contents.html: This Recommendation specifies a deterministic authenticated-encryption mode of operation of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) block cipher [3]. The mode is called AES Key Wrap, abbreviated as KW in this Recommendation. Although KW can be used in conjunction with any reversible padding scheme, a variant of KW with an internal padding scheme is also specified to promote interoperability. This variant is called AES Key Wrap With Padding, abbreviated as KWP. The analogue of KW with the Triple Data Encryption Algorithm (TDEA) [5] as the underlying block cipher is also specified, to support legacy applications. This analogue is called Triple DEA Key Wrap, abbreviated as TKW.
contents.html_ja: 本勧告は、Advanced Encryption Standard（AES）ブロック暗号[3]の決定論的な認証付き暗号化利用モードを規定します。本勧告ではこれをAES Key Wrap（KW）と呼びます。KWは任意の可逆パディング方式と組み合わせて使用できるが、相互運用性を促進するため、内部パディング方式を持つKWの変種も規定します。これをAES Key Wrap With Padding（KWP）と呼びます。また、レガシーアプリケーションを支援するため、基礎ブロック暗号にTriple Data Encryption Algorithm（TDEA）[5]を用いるKWの類似方式も規定します。これをTriple DEA Key Wrap（TKW）と呼びます。

contents.html: KW, KWP, and TKW were designed to protect the confidentiality and the authenticity/integrity of cryptographic keys. Each provides an option for protecting keys in a manner that is distinct from the methods that protect general data. Segregating keys from general data can provide an extra layer of protection.
contents.html_ja: KW、KWP、TKWは、暗号鍵の機密性および真正性／完全性を保護するために設計されました。各方式は一般データの保護方式とは異なる形で鍵を保護する選択肢を提供します。鍵を一般データから分離することで、保護をさらに一層強化できます。

contents.html: Nevertheless, there is no requirement to protect cryptographic keys with a distinct cryptographic method. Previously approved authenticated-encryption modes—as well as combinations of an approved encryption mode with an approved authentication method—are approved for the protection of cryptographic keys, in addition to general data.
contents.html_ja: ただし、暗号鍵を別個の暗号方式で保護する要件はありません。以前に承認された認証付き暗号化モード、および承認済み暗号化モードと承認済み認証方式の組合せは、一般データに加え暗号鍵の保護にも承認されています。

contents.html: Similarly, KW, KWP, and TKW are each approved for the protection of general data, as well as cryptographic keys.
contents.html_ja: KW、KWP、TKWはいずれも、暗号鍵だけでなく一般データの保護にも承認されています。

contents.html: KW, KWP, and TKW are each robust in the sense that each bit of output can be expected to depend in a nontrivial fashion on each bit of input, even when the length of the input data is greater than one block. This property is achieved at the cost of a considerably lower throughput rate, compared to other authenticated-encryption modes, but the tradeoff may be appropriate for some key management applications. For example, a robust method may be desired when the length of the keys to be protected is greater than the block size of the underlying block cipher, or when the value of the protected data is very high.
contents.html_ja: KW、KWP、TKWはいずれも堅牢であり、入力データが1ブロックを超える長さでも、出力の各ビットは入力の各ビットに実質的に依存すると期待できます。この性質は、他の認証付き暗号化モードに比べてスループットが大幅に低くなる代償を伴うが、一部の鍵管理用途ではその交換条件が適切な場合があります。例えば、保護する鍵が基礎ブロック暗号のブロックサイズを超える場合や、保護対象データの価値が非常に高い場合には、堅牢な方式が望まれることがあります。

contents.html: 3.2 Related Specifications
contents.html_ja: 3.2 関連仕様

contents.html: Earlier specifications of key-wrap algorithms<sup>1</sup> that are related to KW, KWP, and TKW are discussed in this subsection.
contents.html_ja: KW、KWP、TKWに関連する以前の鍵ラッピングアルゴリズム仕様<sup>1</sup>を本節で説明します。

contents.html: In 2001, NIST posted a document entitled “AES Key Wrap Specification” on NIST’s Computer Security Resource Center web site as an unofficial suggestion for the protection of cryptographic keys. That algorithm is essentially equivalent to KW as specified in this Recommendation.
contents.html_ja: 2001年、NISTは暗号鍵保護の非公式な提案として「AES Key Wrap Specification」と題する文書をNIST Computer Security Resource Centerのウェブサイトに掲載しました。このアルゴリズムは、本勧告で規定するKWと実質的に同等です。

contents.html: In 2002, two industry groups published specifications of key-wrap algorithms that were based on the specification that NIST posted. First, the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) developed an essentially equivalent specification in Request For Comments (RFC) 3394 [11]. Second, the Telecommunications Industry Association published a protocol for Digital Radio Over-the-Air-Rekeying [1] containing a “Key Wrap Algorithm” that supported TDEA, in addition to the AES block cipher. Those algorithms are essentially equivalent to KW and TKW as specified in this Recommendation.
contents.html_ja: 2002年、2つの業界団体がNIST掲載仕様に基づく鍵ラッピングアルゴリズム仕様を公表しました。まずInternet Engineering Task Force（IETF）が実質的に同等の仕様を開発し、Request For Comments（RFC）3394 [11]として公表しました。次にTelecommunications Industry AssociationはDigital Radio Over-the-Air-Rekeying用プロトコル[1]を公表し、AESに加えてTDEAもサポートする「Key Wrap Algorithm」を含めました。これらのアルゴリズムは、本勧告のKWおよびTKWと実質的に同等です。

contents.html: In 2008, Accredited Standards Committee X9, Inc., published a key-wrap standard for the financial services industry [2]. The variant of KW in that standard features a more general framework for formatting the input data, including a padding scheme, as well as an analogue with TDEA as the underlying block cipher.
contents.html_ja: 2008年、Accredited Standards Committee X9, Inc.は金融サービス業界向け鍵ラッピング標準[2]を公表しました。同標準のKW変種は、パディング方式を含む、入力データ形式のより一般的な枠組みを備え、基礎ブロック暗号にTDEAを用いる類似方式も含みます。

contents.html: 1 The term “algorithm” here indicates a high-level cryptographic technique that may encompass more than one computational procedure; for example, an "encryption algorithm" like TDEA or the AES algorithm has transformations for both encryption and decryption. This publication also contains ten numbered algorithms in the original sense of the word, i.e., as a list of instructions for executing a single computational procedure.
contents.html_ja: ¹ ここで「アルゴリズム」は、複数の計算手順を含み得る上位レベルの暗号技術を指します。例えば、TDEAやAESのような「暗号化アルゴリズム」には、暗号化と復号の両方の変換が含まれます。本刊行物には、単一の計算手順を実行する命令一覧という本来の意味での番号付きアルゴリズムも10個含まれます。

contents.html: In 2009, a different padding scheme was specified in RFC 5649 [4], referencing elements of the specification in [11]. The resulting algorithm, called AES Key Wrap With Padding, is essentially equivalent to KWP as specified in this Recommendation.
contents.html_ja: 2009年、RFC 5649 [4]で別のパディング方式が規定され、[11]の仕様の要素が参照されました。その結果のアルゴリズム AES Key Wrap With Padding は、本勧告のKWPと実質的に同等です。

contents.html: The differences between KW, KWP, and TKW as specified in this Recommendation and their earlier specifications are described in Appendix B.1.
contents.html_ja: 本勧告のKW、KWP、TKWと以前の仕様との相違点は付録B.1で説明します。

contents.html: 4 Definitions and Notation
contents.html_ja: 4 定義および表記

contents.html: 4.1 Definitions
contents.html_ja: 4.1 定義

contents.html:
approvedFIPS-approved or NIST-recommended: an algorithm or technique that is either 1) specified in a FIPS or a NIST Recommendation, or 2) adopted in a FIPS or a NIST Recommendation.
authenticated-encryption functionA function that encrypts plaintext into ciphertext and provides a means for the associated authenticated-decryption function to verify the authenticity and, therefore, the integrity of the data.
authenticated-decryption functionA function that decrypts purported ciphertext into corresponding plaintext and verifies the authenticity and, therefore, the integrity of the data. The output is either the plaintext or an indication that the plaintext is not authentic.
authenticityThe property that data originated from its purported source. In the context of a key-wrap algorithm, the source of authentic data is an entity with access to an implementation of the authenticated-encryption function with the KEK.
bitA binary digit: 0 or 1.
bit stringA finite, ordered sequence of bits.
blockFor a given block cipher, a bit string whose length is the block size of the block cipher.
block cipherA parameterized family of permutations on bit strings of a fixed length; the parameter that determines the permutation is a bit string called the key.

contents.html: The transformations of the variants of KW feature a block cipher as the main component; thus, each variant is a mode of operation (mode, for short) of the block cipher. The key for the underlying block cipher is called the key encryption key (KEK), denoted \(K\).
contents.html_ja: KWの各変種の変換ではブロック暗号が主要な構成要素となります。したがって、各変種はブロック暗号の利用モード（以下、モード）です。基礎となるブロック暗号の鍵を鍵暗号化鍵（KEK）と呼び、\(K\) と表します。

contents.html: For any given KEK, the underlying block cipher of the mode is a permutation, i.e., an invertible transformation on bit strings of a fixed length. In this publication, the transformation is called the forward transformation, and its inverse is called the inverse transformation. The strings are called blocks, and the length of a block is called the block size. As part of the choice of the underlying block cipher with the KEK, either the forward transformation or the inverse transformation is specified as the designated cipher function, denoted \(\mathrm{CIPH}_K\). The inverse of \(\mathit{CIPH}_K\) is denoted \(\mathrm{CIPH}^{-1}_K\).
contents.html_ja: KEKごとに、モードの基礎となるブロック暗号は置換、すなわち固定長ビット列上の可逆変換です。本書では変換を順変換、その逆を逆変換と呼びます。ビット列をブロック、ブロックの長さをブロックサイズと呼びます。KEKと基礎ブロック暗号を選択する際、順変換または逆変換のいずれかを指定暗号関数として指定し、\(\mathrm{CIPH}_K\)と表します。\(\mathit{CIPH}_K\)の逆関数を\(\mathrm{CIPH}^{-1}_K\)と表します。

contents.html: For a given KEK and block cipher, KW, KWP, and TKW each comprise two related functions: authenticated encryption and authenticated decryption. The authenticated-encryption function takes an input string, called the plaintext, denoted \(P\), and returns a longer output string, called the ciphertext, denoted \(C\). The authenticated-encryption function expands the data so that only a small fraction of all possible strings of any given length can be ciphertexts.
contents.html_ja: 所与のKEKとブロック暗号に対し、KW、KWP、TKWはいずれも関連する2つの関数、すなわち認証付き暗号化と認証付き復号から成ります。認証付き暗号化関数は、平文と呼び\(P\)と表す入力文字列を取り、暗号文と呼び\(C\)と表す、より長い出力文字列を返します。認証付き暗号化関数はデータを拡張するため、任意の所与の長さのすべての文字列のうち、暗号文となり得るものはごく一部に限られます。

contents.html: The authenticated-decryption function takes an input string, called the purported ciphertext, and returns either 1) an output string or 2) a special symbol, denoted FAIL. In the first case, the output string is the unique plaintext that corresponds to the purported ciphertext, so the ciphertext should be regarded as authentic; the nature of the resulting assurance is described in Appendix A.3.
contents.html_ja: 認証付き復号関数は「暗号文とされる」入力文字列を取り、1) 出力文字列または2) FAILと表す特別な記号のいずれかを返します。前者の場合、出力文字列は当該暗号文とされる文字列に対応する一意の平文であるため、その暗号文は真正と見なすべきです。保証の性質は付録A.3で説明します。

contents.html: For KW, the authenticated-encryption function and the authenticated-decryption function are denoted KW-AE and KW-AD; for KWP, the functions are denoted KWP-AE and KWP-AD; for TKW, the functions are denoted TKW-AE and TKW-AD.
contents.html_ja: KWでは認証付き暗号化関数と認証付き復号関数をKW-AEおよびKW-AD、KWPではKWP-AEおよびKWP-AD、TKWではTKW-AEおよびTKW-ADと表します。

contents.html: Note that, although the KEK, K, is a parameter for each of these six functions, in the specifications of these functions in this Recommendation, the KEK is considered to be a prerequisite, i.e., an input that has been established prior to the invocation of the function, and is omitted from the notation. Similarly, the choice of the block cipher for the KW and the KWP functions and the designation of CIPH<sub>K</sub> are prerequisites that are omitted from the notation.

contents.html: The authenticated-encryption and authenticated-decryption functions of KW and KWP are based on a keyed transformation, called the wrapping function, denoted \(\mathrm{W}\), and its inverse, called the unwrapping function, denoted \(\mathrm{W}^{-1}\). The analogous keyed transformations for TKW are denoted \(\mathrm{TW}\) and \(\mathrm{TW}^{-1}\).
contents.html_ja: KWおよびKWPの認証付き暗号化関数と認証付き復号関数は、鍵付き変換であるラッピング関数（\(\mathrm{W}\)と表す）と、その逆変換であるアンラッピング関数（\(\mathrm{W}^{-1}\)と表す）に基づきます。TKWに対応する鍵付き変換は\(\mathrm{TW}\)および\(\mathrm{TW}^{-1}\)と表します。

contents.html: Within the authenticated-encryption function, the wrapping function is applied to an enlarged plaintext string to produce the ciphertext. Each key-wrap variant enlarges the plaintext by prepending a fixed string called the integrity check value (ICV); for KWP-AE, the enlarged plaintext also includes a 32-bit encoding of the octet length of the plaintext and possibly some “zero” octets as padding.

contents.html: In each key-wrap variant, the authenticated-decryption function applies the unwrapping function to the purported ciphertext and then verifies whether the output string is the result of properly enlarging a plaintext string.
contents.html_ja: 各鍵ラッピング変種の認証付き復号関数は、暗号文とされる文字列にアンラッピング関数を適用し、その出力が平文文字列を正しく拡張した結果かどうかを検証します。

contents.html: A useful unit of length for describing these functions is half the block size, i.e., 64 bits for KW and KWP, and 32 bits for TKW. A bit string of this length is called a semiblock, and, for a non-negative integer n, the term “n semiblocks” means a bit string that can be represented as the concatenation of n semiblocks , or, alternatively, a semiblock string of length n.
contents.html_ja: これらの関数を記述する際に便利な長さの単位はブロックサイズの半分であり、KWおよびKWPでは64ビット、TKWでは32ビットです。この長さのビット列をセミブロックと呼びます。非負整数nに対する「nセミブロック」とは、n個のセミブロックを連結して表せるビット列、すなわち長さnのセミブロック列を意味します。

contents.html: For each key-wrap variant, the wrapping function and the unwrapping function are invoked on three or more semiblocks, although in principle, the definition could be extended to inputs of two semiblocks. The length of the output is the same as the length of the input for both functions.

contents.html:
Algorithm 1: \(\operatorname{W}(S)\)

Prerequisites:
KEK, \(K\), for an approved, 128-bit block cipher;
designated cipher function, \(\operatorname{CIPH}_K\).

Input:
a string, \(S\), of \(n\) semiblocks, for some integer \(n\ge3\).

Steps:

  1. Initialize variables.
    1. Let \(s=6(n-1)\).
    2. Let \(S_1,S_2,\ldots,S_n\) be the semiblocks such that \(S=S_1\parallel S_2\parallel\ldots\parallel S_n\).
    3. Let \(A^0=S_1\).
    4. For \(i=2,\ldots,n\): let \(R_i^0=S_i\).
  2. Calculate the intermediate values. For \(t=1,\ldots,s\), update the variables as follows:
    1. \[A^t=\operatorname{MSB}_{64}(\operatorname{CIPH}_K(A^{t-1}\parallel R_2^{t-1}))\oplus[t]_{64};\]
    2. For \(i=2,\ldots,n-1\): \(R_i^t=R_{i+1}^{t-1}\);
    3. \[R_n^t=\operatorname{LSB}_{64}(\operatorname{CIPH}_K(A^{t-1}\parallel R_2^{t-1})).\]
  3. Output the results:
    1. Let \(C_1=A^s\).
    2. For \(i=2,\ldots,n\): \(C_i=R_i^s\).
    3. Return \(C_1\parallel C_2\parallel\ldots\parallel C_n\).

アルゴリズム1：\(\operatorname{W}(S)\)

事前条件：
承認済み128ビットブロック暗号のKEK \(K\)；

入力：

    2. \(S_1,S_2,\ldots,S_n\)を、\(S=S_1\parallel S_2\parallel\ldots\parallel S_n\)となるセミブロックとします。
    3. \(A^0=S_1\)とします。
    4. \(i=2,\ldots,n\)について、\(R_i^0=S_i\)とします。
  2. 中間値を計算します。\(t=1,\ldots,s\)について、変数を次のように更新する：
    1. \[A^t=\operatorname{MSB}_{64}(\operatorname{CIPH}_K(A^{t-1}\parallel R_2^{t-1}))\oplus[t]_{64};\]

  3. 結果を出力する：
    1. \(C_1=A^s\)とします。
    2. \(i=2,\ldots,n\)について、\(C_i=R_i^s\)。
    3. \(C_1\parallel C_2\parallel\ldots\parallel C_n\)を返します。

Algorithm 2: \(\mathrm{W}^{-1}(C)\)

Prerequisites:

inverse of the designated cipher function, \(\mathrm{CIPH}^{-1}_{K}\).

Input:

Steps:

Algorithm 7: \(\mathrm{TW}(S)\)

Prerequisites:
KEK, \(K\), for TDEA;
designated cipher function, \(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}\).

Input:
a string, \(S\), of \(n\) semiblocks, for some integer \(n \ge 3\).

Steps:

  1. Initialize the variables.
    1. Let \(s = 6(n-1)\).
    2. Let \(S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n\) be the semiblocks such that \(S = S_1 \parallel S_2 \parallel \ldots \parallel S_n\).
    3. Let \(A^{0} = S_1\).
    4. For \(i = 2, \ldots, n\), let \(R_i^{0} = S_i\).
  2. Calculate the intermediate values. For \(t = 1, \ldots, \mathrm{s}\), update the variables as follows:
    1. \(A^{t} = \mathrm{MSB}_{32}(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}(A^{t-1} \parallel R_2^{t-1})) \oplus [t]_{32}\);
    2. For \(i = 2, \ldots, n-1\): \(R_i^{t} = R_{i+1}^{t-1}\);
    3. \(R_n^{t} = \mathrm{LSB}_{32}(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}(A^{t-1} \parallel R_2^{t-1}))\).

contents.html: Appendix A: Some Security Considerations
contents.html_ja: 付録A：セキュリティ上のいくつかの考慮事項

contents.html: A.1 Equality of Plaintexts
contents.html_ja: A.1 平文の同一性

contents.html: Each key-wrap algorithm in this Recommendation is deterministic: for a given designated cipher function and KEK, any invocation of the authenticated-encryption function on a given plaintext produces the same ciphertext. It follows that any pair of ciphertexts reveals whether the corresponding plaintexts are equal.
contents.html_ja: 本勧告の各鍵ラッピングアルゴリズムは決定論的です。すなわち、指定暗号関数とKEKを固定すると、同じ平文に認証付き暗号化関数を呼び出すたびに同じ暗号文が生成されます。したがって、任意の2つの暗号文を比較すれば、対応する平文が同一かどうかが分かります。

contents.html: Therefore, ideally, for a given designated cipher function and KEK, the authenticated-encryption function should be invoked only once on each plaintext. If multiple invocations are necessary on the same data for a system, then one method for ensuring that the ciphertexts are different would be to prepend the data with a fixed-length nonce before invoking the authenticated-encryption function. Upon authenticated decryption, the nonce would be discarded.
contents.html_ja: したがって理想的には、指定暗号関数とKEKを固定し、各平文に対する認証付き暗号化関数の呼出しは1回だけにすべきです。システム上、同じデータに複数回呼び出す必要がある場合、関数の呼出し前に固定長nonceをデータの前に付加すれば、暗号文を異なるものにできます。認証付き復号時にnonceを破棄します。

contents.html: A.2 Implied Strength of Protected Keys
contents.html_ja: A.2 保護される鍵の暗黙の強度

contents.html: The disclosure of a KEK potentially compromises any data (i.e., any key) that the KEK protects. Therefore, the cryptographic strength of the protected key is limited implicitly by the resistance of the KEK to brute force search, and this resistance is limited by the length of the KEK. To maintain the expected level of assurance, the generation and management of the KEK should be at least as strong cryptographically as any key that it protects.
contents.html_ja: KEKが開示されると、KEKが保護するデータ（すなわち鍵）が侵害される可能性があります。したがって、保護対象鍵の暗号強度は、総当たり探索へのKEKの耐性によって暗黙に制限され、その耐性はKEKの長さによって制限されます。期待する保証レベルを維持するには、KEKの生成および管理の暗号強度を、保護対象のいずれの鍵と比べても同等以上にすべきです。

contents.html: A.3 Authentication Assurance
contents.html_ja: A.3 認証保証

contents.html: The expansion of the plaintext within the authenticated-encryption function provides the mechanism whereby assurance of the authenticity of the data can be obtained when the authenticated-decryption function is invoked. The nature of this assurance depends on the output of the authenticated-decryption function:
contents.html_ja: 認証付き暗号化関数内で平文を拡張することにより、認証付き復号関数の呼出し時にデータの真正性を保証する仕組みが得られます。この保証の性質は認証付き復号関数の出力によって異なります。

contents.html: If the output is a plaintext, i.e., not FAIL, then the design of the mode provides strong, but not absolute, assurance of the authenticity of the data, i.e., that the ciphertext was generated by an invocation of the authenticated-encryption function on the plaintext. The authenticity implies the integrity of the ciphertext and resulting plaintext, i.e., that they were not altered, intentionally or unintentionally, after the generation of the ciphertext.
contents.html_ja: 出力が平文、すなわちFAILでない場合、このモード設計は、データの真正性、つまりその平文に対する認証付き暗号化関数の呼出しによって暗号文が生成されたことを強く保証します。ただし絶対的な保証ではありません。真正性は暗号文と復号後の平文の完全性、すなわち暗号文生成後に意図的または偶発的に改変されていないことを含意します。

contents.html: • If the output is \(\mathit{FAIL}\), then it is certain that the ciphertext is not authentic.
contents.html_ja: • 出力が \(\mathit{FAIL}\) の場合、その暗号文が真正でないことは確実です。

contents.html: In the first case, the assurance is not absolute because forgeries are possible, in principle. In other words, an adversary, without access to the key or to an implementation of the authenticated-encryption function, may be able to produce a genuine ciphertext, for example, by a lucky guess.
contents.html_ja: 前者の場合、原理上、偽造が可能であるため保証は絶対ではありません。つまり、鍵にも認証付き暗号化関数の実装にもアクセスできない攻撃者が、例えば偶然の推測によって真正な暗号文を生成できる可能性があります。

contents.html: In particular, if the adversary chooses a string at random with a valid ciphertext length, the probability that the string will be a genuine ciphertext is exactly 1 in \(2^{64}\) for KW, and approximately 1 in \(2^{64}\) for KWP. The probability that a randomly chosen ciphertext will appear to be genuine for TKW is greater, 1 in \(2^{32}\), so TKW is significantly more vulnerable to forgeries.

contents.html: For this reason, TKW is not recommended for new applications.
contents.html_ja: このため、新規アプリケーションにはTKWを推奨しません。

contents.html: Given repeated attempts, of course, the adversary can increase the probability that a randomly-generated string will eventually be accepted as a valid ciphertext. The system or protocol that implements the authenticated-decryption function should monitor and, if necessary, limit the number of unsuccessful verification attempts for each key.

contents.html: A.4 Forgeries of Extremely Long Messages

contents.html:
The motivation for the limits on the length of the plaintext in Sec. 5.3 is the following observation on the unwrapping function, due to John Kelsey of NIST: if \(S\) is extremely long, about \(2^{67}\) semiblocks, and if \(T\) and \(U\) are semiblock strings of equal length, it is likely that

\[ \mathrm{MSB}_{64d}(\mathrm{W}^{-1}(S \parallel T)) = \mathrm{MSB}_{64d}(\mathrm{W}^{-1}(S \parallel U)) \tag{1} \]

for some positive integer \(d\).
contents.html_ja:

\[ \mathrm{MSB}_{64d}(\mathrm{W}^{-1}(S \parallel T)) = \mathrm{MSB}_{64d}(\mathrm{W}^{-1}(S \parallel U)) \tag{1} \]

ここで \(d\) はある正の整数です。

contents.html: In particular, let \(S\) be a semiblock string of length \(m\), and let \(T\) and \(U\) be distinct semiblocks. contents.html: Within [10], Rogaway and Shrimpton provide an analysis of AESKW as specified in [2], much of which also applies to the key-wrap variants in this Recommendation. Among other criticisms, the authors emphasize the lack of a proof that the underlying structure of KW meets the goal of deterministic authenticated encryption that they formalize in the paper. Nevertheless, the authors expect that the AES Key Wrap achieves this property, possibly even in a particularly strong manner, i.e., with “beyond-birthday-phenomenon security.”
contents.html_ja: [10]でRogawayとShrimptonは、[2]に規定されたAESKWの分析を示しており、その多くは本勧告の鍵ラッピング変種にも当てはまります。著者らは、他の批判の中でも、KWの基礎構造が、本論文で形式化した決定論的認証付き暗号化の目標を満たすことの証明がない点を強調します。それでも著者らは、AES Key Wrapがこの性質を、場合によっては特に強い形で、すなわち「birthday現象を超える安全性」を伴って満たすと期待しています。

contents.html: B.1 Technical Differences With Earlier Specifications of Key-Wrap Algorithms
contents.html_ja: B.1 以前の鍵ラッピングアルゴリズム仕様との技術的差異

contents.html: Two features that are unique to this Recommendation are: 1) the maximum plaintext lengths for KW and TKW in Sec 5.3.1, and 2) the explicit option for implementation-specific subsets of valid lengths for KW, KWP, and TKW in Sec. 5.3.2. In particular, KW-AE, KWP-AE, and TKW-AE are undefined on plaintexts of invalid length, while KW-AD, KWP-AD, and TKW-AD check whether the length of the purported ciphertext is valid.
contents.html_ja: 本勧告独自の特徴は、1) セクション5.3.1のKWおよびTKWの平文長上限、2) セクション5.3.2のKW、KWP、TKWに対する実装固有の有効長部分集合の明示的な選択肢です。特に、KW-AE、KWP-AE、TKW-AEは無効長の平文に対して未定義である一方、KW-AD、KWP-AD、TKW-ADは暗号文とされる入力の長さが有効かどうかを検査します。

contents.html: This Recommendation also differs slightly in its support of underlying block ciphers. The AES Key Wrap, both in the original “AES Key Wrap Specification” that was posted on NIST’s Computer Security Resource Center web site and also in [11], is defined only for the AES block cipher; however, KW and KWP will also support any 128-bit block cipher that is approved in the future. The “Key Wrap” algorithm in [1] supports a wider choice of block ciphers, encompassing a variant that is equivalent to TKW, but also allowing TDEA with key lengths that are not supported in TKW.
contents.html_ja: 本勧告は基礎ブロック暗号のサポートについても多少異なります。NIST Computer Security Resource Centerウェブサイトに掲載された当初の「AES Key Wrap Specification」も[11]も、AESブロック暗号のみを対象とします。一方、KWおよびKWPは将来承認される128ビットブロック暗号もサポートします。[1]の「Key Wrap」アルゴリズムはより幅広いブロック暗号をサポートし、TKWと同等の変種に加え、TKWではサポートされない鍵長のTDEAも許容します。

contents.html: Otherwise, the specification of KW in this Recommendation is equivalent to the original “AES Key Wrap Specification” and to the specification in [11], and almost equivalent to the “Key Wrap” specification in [1]. The specification in [1] supports the appending of random padding bits to plaintexts that are not semiblock strings, when the length of plaintext is fixed. This amounts to a reversible padding scheme that is different than the padding scheme defined in [4] and later adopted for KWP.
contents.html_ja: それ以外の点では、本勧告のKW仕様は当初の「AES Key Wrap Specification」および[11]の仕様と同等であり、[1]の「Key Wrap」仕様ともほぼ同等です。[1]の仕様は、平文長が固定されている場合、セミブロック列でない平文にランダムなパディングビットを付加することを認めます。これは[4]で定義され、後にKWPに採用された方式とは異なる可逆パディング方式です。

contents.html: In [2], an analogue of KWP and an analogue of TKW are defined. The wrapping and unwrapping functions for these analogues are equivalent to \(\mathrm{W}\), \(\mathrm{W}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{TW}\), and \(\mathrm{TW}^{-1}\), but the formatting of the plaintext is different, so implementations of the key-wrap algorithms in [2] cannot be compliant with this Recommendation.

contents.html: B.2 Comparison of Functionality with Other Authentication Methods
contents.html_ja: B.2 他の認証方式との機能比較

contents.html: The authentication assurance that KW-AD, KWP-AD, and TKW-AD each provide is described in Appendix A.3 above; that assurance is similar to the authentication assurance that other methods provide via the verification of an authentication tag, i.e., a digital signature or a message authentication code (MAC). Therefore, a digital signature or a MAC is not necessary to authenticate the data that is protected by a key-wrap algorithm.
contents.html_ja: KW-AD、KWP-AD、TKW-ADがそれぞれ提供する認証保証は上記付録A.3に記述したとおりであり、その保証は、他の方式が認証タグ、すなわちデジタル署名またはメッセージ認証コード（MAC）の検証によって提供する認証保証と同様です。したがって、鍵ラッピングアルゴリズムで保護されるデータを認証するために、デジタル署名やMACは必要ありません。

contents.html: However, other authentication methods differ from KW, KWP, and TKW in at least three properties: 1) Digital signatures provide non-repudiation. 2) Many authenticated-encryption algorithms, including the Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) [6] and the Counter with Cipher Block Chaining Mode (CCM) [5], provide an efficient means of authenticating associated data that is not confidential, such as the routing information in a networking protocol, or the description of the usage of the protected key. 3) Digital signatures on ciphertexts or MACs on ciphertexts can be verified without decrypting the ciphertext.<sup>2</sup> By contrast, for KW, KWP, and TKW, there are no separate authentication tags: instead, the information that is necessary to verify the authenticity of the data is embedded in all of the ciphertext bits. Consequently, for these three algorithms, the authenticity of the data cannot be verified without invoking the authenticated-decryption function.
contents.html_ja: ただし、他の認証方式は少なくとも3点でKW、KWP、TKWと異なります。1) デジタル署名は否認防止を提供します。2) Galois/Counter Mode（GCM）[6]およびCounter with Cipher Block Chaining Mode（CCM）[5]を含む多くの認証付き暗号化アルゴリズムは、ネットワークプロトコルの経路情報や保護鍵の用途の説明など、機密ではない関連データを効率的に認証できます。3) 暗号文に対するデジタル署名またはMACは、暗号文を復号せずに検証できます。<sup>2</sup>これに対しKW、KWP、TKWには独立した認証タグがなく、データの真正性検証に必要な情報は暗号文の全ビットに埋め込まれています。したがって、これら3アルゴリズムでは認証付き復号関数を呼び出さずにデータの真正性を検証できません。

contents.html: 2 This statement applies to the internal MAC of GCM, but not to the internal MAC of CCM, which is generated on the plaintext.
contents.html_ja: ² この記述はGCMの内部MACには当てはまるが、平文上に生成されるCCMの内部MACには当てはまりません。

original_blocks.html: The transformations of the variants of KW feature a block cipher as the main component; thus, each variant is a mode of operation (mode, for short) of the block cipher. The key for the underlying block cipher is called the key encryption key (KEK), denoted K.

original_blocks.html: For example, the forward and inverse transformations for the AES block cipher—called “cipher” and “inverse cipher” in [3]—are informally known as the AES encryption and AES decryption functions, respectively. If the designated cipher function for a key-wrap algorithm is chosen to be the AES decryption function, then CIPH<sup>−1</sup><sub>K</sub> will be the AES encryption function.
original_blocks.html_ja: 例えば、AESブロック暗号の順変換および逆変換は、[3]ではそれぞれ「cipher」および「inverse cipher」と呼ばれるが、非公式にはそれぞれAES暗号化関数およびAES復号関数として知られている。鍵ラッピングアルゴリズムの指定暗号関数としてAES復号関数を選んだ場合、CIPH<sup>−1</sup><sub>K</sub>はAES暗号化関数となる。

original_blocks.html: For a given KEK and block cipher, KW, KWP, and TKW each comprise two related functions: authenticated encryption and authenticated decryption. The authenticated-encryption function takes an input string, called the plaintext, denoted P, and returns a longer output string, called the ciphertext, denoted C. The authenticated-encryption function expands the data so that only a small fraction of all possible strings of any given length can be ciphertexts.

In this publication, the Courier New font indicates the “0” bit, the “1” bit, and any hexadecimal symbols: 0, 1, …, 9, A, B, C, D, E, F.

The beginning of a hexadecimal representation of a string is marked by “0x.” For example, 0xA659 = 1010011001011001.

Given a real number x, the ceiling function, denoted ⌈x⌉, is the least integer that is not less than x. For example, ⌈2.1⌉ = 3, and ⌈4⌉ = 4.

Given a positive integer s, 0s denotes the string that consists of s “0” bits. For example, 08 = 00000000.

The concatenation operation on bit strings is denoted ||. For example, 001 || 10111 = 00110111.

Given bit strings of equal length, the exclusive-OR (XOR) operation, denoted ⊕, specifies the addition, modulo 2, of the bits in corresponding bit positions. For example, 10011 ⊕ 10101 = 00110.

文字列の16進表記は「0x」で始まる。例えば、0xA659 = 1010011001011001である。

実数xに対し、天井関数⌈x⌉はx以上である最小の整数を表す。例えば、⌈2.1⌉ = 3、⌈4⌉ = 4である。

ビット列の連結演算を||と表す。例えば、001 || 10111 = 00110111である。

同じ長さのビット列に対する排他的論理和（XOR）演算を⊕と表し、対応する位置のビットを法2で加算する。例えば、10011 ⊕ 10101 = 00110である。

Given a bit string X, the bit length of X is denoted len(X). For example, len(00010) = 5.

Given a bit string X and a non-negative integer s such that len(X) ≥ s, the functions LSBs(X) and MSBs(X) return the s least significant (right-most) bits and the s most significant (left-most) bits, respectively, of X. For example, LSB3(111011010) = 010, and MSB4(111011010) = 1110.

Given a positive integer s and a non-negative integer x that is less than 2s, the integer-to-string function, denoted [x]s, is the binary representation of x as a string of bit length s with the least significant bit on the right. For example, for the (base 10) integer 39, the binary representation (base 2) is 100111, so [39]8 = 00100111.

Given a (non-empty) bit string X, the string-to-integer function, denoted int(X), is the integer x such that [x]len(X) = X. In other words, int(X) is the non-negative integer less than 2len(X) whose binary representation is X. For example, int(00011010) = 26.

Algorithm 2: W−1(C)
Prerequisites: KEK, K, for an approved 128-bit block cipher; inverse of the designated cipher function CIPH−1K.
Input: a string C of n semiblocks, for some integer n ≥ 3.
Output: the unwrapped string W−1(C).
Steps:
  1. Initialize the variables:
    1. Let s = 6(n−1).
    2. Let C1, C2, …, Cn be the semiblocks such that C = C1 || C2 || … || Cn.
    3. Let As = C1.
    4. For i = 2, …, n: let Ris = Ci.
  2. Calculate the intermediate values. For t = s, s−1, …, 1, update the variables as follows:
    1. At−1 = MSB64(CIPH−1K((At ⊕ [t]64) || Rnt)).
    2. R2t−1 = LSB64(CIPH−1K((At ⊕ [t]64) || Rnt)).
    3. For i = 2, …, n−1: Ri+1t−1 = Rit.
  3. Output the results:
    1. Let S1 = A0.
    2. For i = 2, …, n: Si = Ri0.
    3. Return S = S1 || S2 || … || Sn.

入力：n ≥ 3である整数nについて、n個のセミブロックからなる文字列C。
出力：アンラップ済み文字列W−1(C)。
手順：
  1. 変数を初期化する。
    1. s = 6(n−1)とする。
    2. C = C1 || C2 || … || CnとなるセミブロックC1, C2, …, Cnを定める。

Prerequisites: KEK, K, for an approved 128-bit block cipher; designated cipher function CIPHK; definition of valid plaintext lengths.
Input: plaintext P, with valid length.
Output: ciphertext C.
Steps:
  1. Let ICV2 = 0xA65959A6.
  2. Let padlen = 8⌈len(P)/64⌉ − len(P)/8.
  3. Let PAD = 08·padlen.
  4. Let S = ICV2 || [len(P)/8]32 || P || PAD.
  5. If len(P) ≤ 64, then return C = CIPHK(S); if len(P) > 64, then return C = W(S).

入力：有効長の平文P。
出力：暗号文C。

  2. padlen = 8⌈len(P)/64⌉ − len(P)/8とする。

Algorithm 7: TW(S)
Prerequisites: KEK, K, for TDEA; designated cipher function CIPHK.
Input: a string S of n semiblocks, for some integer n ≥ 3.
Output: the wrapped string TW(S).
Steps:
  1. Initialize variables:
    1. Let s = 6(n−1).
    2. Let S1, S2, …, Sn be the semiblocks such that S = S1 || S2 || … || Sn.
    3. Let A0 = S1.
    4. For i = 2, …, n, let Ri0 = Si.
  2. Calculate the intermediate values. For t = 1, …, s, update the variables as follows:
    1. At = MSB32(CIPHK(At−1 || R2t−1)) ⊕ [t]32.
    2. For i = 2, …, n−1: Rit = Ri+1t−1.
    3. Rnt = LSB32(CIPHK(At−1 || R2t−1)).
  3. Output the results:
    1. Let C1 = As.
    2. For i = 2, …, n: Ci = Ris.
    3. Return C = C1 || C2 || … || Cn.

    4. i = 2, …, nについてRi0 = Siとする。
  2. 中間値を計算する。t = 1, …, sについて以下のように更新する。

    3. Rnt = LSB32(CIPHK(At−1 || R2t−1))とする。
  3. 結果を出力する。
    1. C1 = Asとする。
    2. i = 2, …, nについてCi = Risとする。

Algorithm 10: TKW-AD(C)
Prerequisites: KEK, K, for TDEA; inverse of the designated cipher function CIPH−1K; definition of valid ciphertext lengths.
Input: purported ciphertext C, with valid length.
Output: plaintext P or indication of inauthenticity, FAIL.

The motivation for the limits on the length of the plaintext in Sec. 5.3 is the following observation on the unwrapping function, due to John Kelsey of NIST: if S is extremely long, about 267 semiblocks, and if T and U are semiblock strings of equal length, it is likely that
MSB64d(W−1(S || T)) = MSB64d(W−1(S || U))   (1)

for some positive integer d.

セクション5.3の平文長制限の根拠は、NISTのJohn Kelseyによるアンラッピング関数についての次の観察である。Sが非常に長く（約267セミブロック）、TとUが同じ長さのセミブロック列である場合、ある正の整数dについて次が成り立つ可能性が高い。
MSB64d(W−1(S || T)) = MSB64d(W−1(S || U))   (1)

original_blocks.html: The first semiblock of the output of the unwrapping function determines whether a purported ciphertext will pass the integrity check within the authenticated-decryption function. Therefore, if S || T is a given ciphertext for KW, then the modified ciphertext S || U will also pass the integrity check, provided that the collision conditions are satisfied. In other words, if six suitable collisions occur, S || U will be a successful forgery. Moreover, the first i<sub>1</sub>−1 semiblocks of the resulting plaintext will be identical to the plaintext from which S || T was generated.
original_blocks.html_ja: アンラッピング関数の出力の最初のセミブロックにより、暗号文候補が認証付き復号関数の完全性検査に合格するかが決まる。したがって、S || TがKWの暗号文であり、衝突条件を満たすなら、変更後の暗号文S || Uも完全性検査に合格する。つまり、適切な衝突が6個起これば、S || Uは偽造に成功する。さらに、結果の平文の最初のi<sub>1</sub>−1セミブロックは、S || Tの生成元となった平文と同一である。

This procedure will consider exactly m indices; if it identifies collisions at six or more indices, then the first six collisions will satisfy the collision conditions. Conversely, if there are six indices that satisfy the collision conditions, then this procedure will identify collisions at six or more indices. Consequently, for KW, the probability, P, that the forgery attack succeeds in this model is
P = 1 − Σi=05 C(m,i)(1/264)i((264−1)/264)m−i = Σi=6m C(m,i)(1/264)i((264−1)/264)m−i.

original_blocks.html: For any given KEK, the underlying block cipher of the mode is a permutation, i.e., an invertible transformation on bit strings of a fixed length. In this publication, the transformation is called the forward transformation, and its inverse is called the inverse transformation. The strings are called blocks, and the length of a block is called the block size. As part of the choice of the underlying block cipher with the KEK, either the forward transformation or the inverse transformation is specified as the designated cipher function, denoted CIPH<sub>K</sub>. The inverse of CIPH<sub>K</sub> is denoted CIPH<sup>−1</sup><sub>K</sub>.
original_blocks.html_ja: KEKごとに、モードの基礎となるブロック暗号は置換、すなわち固定長ビット列上の可逆変換である。本書では変換を順変換、その逆を逆変換と呼ぶ。文字列をブロック、ブロックの長さをブロックサイズと呼ぶ。KEKと基礎ブロック暗号を選択する際、順変換または逆変換のいずれかを指定暗号関数CIPH<sub>K</sub>として指定する。CIPH<sub>K</sub>の逆関数をCIPH<sup>−1</sup><sub>K</sub>と表す。

Input: purported ciphertext C, with valid length.
Output: plaintext P or indication of inauthenticity, FAIL.

  9. Return P = MSB8·Plen(LSB64(n−1)(S)).

Algorithm 5: \(\text{KWP-AE}(P)\)

Prerequisites:
KEK, \(K\), for an approved, 128-bit block cipher;
designated cipher function, \(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}\);
definition of valid plaintext lengths.

Input:
plaintext \(P\), with valid length.

Output:
ciphertext C.

Steps:

  1. Let \(\mathit{ICV2} = \mathrm{0x}\mathtt{A65959A6}\).
  2. Let \(\mathit{padlen} = 8 \cdot \lceil \operatorname{len}(P)/64 \rceil - \operatorname{len}(P)/8\).
  3. Let \(\mathit{PAD} = \mathtt{0}^{8\mathit{padlen}}\).
  4. Let \(S = \mathit{ICV2} \parallel [\operatorname{len}(P)/8]_{32} \parallel P \parallel \mathit{PAD}\).
  5. If \(\operatorname{len}(P) \le 64\), then return \(C = \mathrm{CIPH}_{K}(S)\); if \(\operatorname{len}(P) > 64\), then return \(C = \mathrm{W}(S)\).

original_blocks.html:
Algorithm 7: \(\mathrm{TW}(S)\)

Prerequisites:
KEK, \(K\), for TDEA;
designated cipher function, \(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}\).

Input:
a string, \(S\), of \(n\) semiblocks, for some integer \(n \ge 3\).

Steps:

  1. Initialize the variables.
    1. Let \(s = 6(n-1)\).
    2. Let \(S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n\) be the semiblocks such that \(S = S_1 \parallel S_2 \parallel \ldots \parallel S_n\).
    3. Let \(A^{0} = S_1\).
    4. For \(i = 2, \ldots, n\), let \(R_i^{0} = S_i\).
  2. Calculate the intermediate values. For \(t = 1, \ldots, \mathrm{s}\), update the variables as follows:
    1. \(A^{t} = \mathrm{MSB}_{32}(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}(A^{t-1} \parallel R_2^{t-1})) \oplus [t]_{32}\);
    2. For \(i = 2, \ldots, n-1\): \(R_i^{t} = R_{i+1}^{t-1}\);
    3. \(R_n^{t} = \mathrm{LSB}_{32}(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}(A^{t-1} \parallel R_2^{t-1}))\).
  3. Output the results:
    1. Let \(C_1 = A^{s}\).
    2. For \(i = 2, \ldots, n\): \(C_i = R_i^{s}\).
    3. Return \(C_1 \parallel C_2 \parallel \ldots \parallel C_n\).

アルゴリズム7：\(\mathrm{TW}(S)\)

前提条件：
TDEAのKEK \(K\)、
指定暗号関数 \(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}\)。

入力：
文字列 \(S\)。\(n\) 個のセミブロックからなり、\(n \ge 3\) は整数である。

手順：

  1. 変数を初期化する。
    1. \(s = 6(n-1)\) とする。
    2. \(S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n\) を、\(S = S_1 \parallel S_2 \parallel \ldots \parallel S_n\) となるセミブロックとする。
    3. \(A^{0} = S_1\) とする。
    4. \(i = 2, \ldots, n\) について、\(R_i^{0} = S_i\) とする。
  2. 中間値を計算する。\(t = 1, \ldots, \mathrm{s}\) について、変数を以下のように更新する。
    1. \(A^{t} = \mathrm{MSB}_{32}(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}(A^{t-1} \parallel R_2^{t-1})) \oplus [t]_{32}\)；
    2. \(i = 2, \ldots, n-1\) について、\(R_i^{t} = R_{i+1}^{t-1}\)；
    3. \(R_n^{t} = \mathrm{LSB}_{32}(\mathrm{CIPH}_{K}(A^{t-1} \parallel R_2^{t-1}))\)。
  3. 結果を出力する。
    1. \(C_1 = A^{s}\) とする。
    2. \(i = 2, \ldots, n\) について、\(C_i = R_i^{s}\)。
    3. \(C_1 \parallel C_2 \parallel \ldots \parallel C_n\) を返す。
